svg.text: Colour marks the purpose coded in the ledger, not whether a place was dug. Bars ignore gaps between seasons.
Computed from searches.csv; totals equal summary.json.
Blue (8): the README's four deposit searches and three
scroll-motivated rows, plus S11, the 1986 re-excavation of
Cave 3Q, the scroll's find site. Grey: all other rows,
14 of 27 rows (52%) have an entry. Rule: the field's first
clause does not say “not given”, “not reported” or “not
7 of 27 (26%) give a depth in m, cm or feet, or say
bedrock was reached: S07, S11, S13, S14, S17, S20 and S21.
S05 (stopped at the Roman floor) and S09 (a deposit
several metres deep) describe depth without a figure.
8 of 27 searches had a scroll-related purpose; 4 were
aimed at the scroll's deposits (S03, S14, S15 and S17).
3 came back negative (S03, S10 and S17), all
scroll-related. Only S17 gives a depth (bedrock); its row
is CLAIM-grade, from blog reports only.
Both claimed finds (S13 and S14) are CLAIM-grade rows. Of
All 17 manuscript surveys and place excavations report
research/history/salvage_records: searches.csv (27 rows), README.md (search ledger section),
summary.json. Each row cites its own pages (source_ids, documentation). S04–S05 date notes: Allegro,
Search in the Desert (1966) pp. 2–3, 37, 158, 164; Rasmussen et al. 2022 p. 2.
Partial dates cover their whole period (“1959” = all of 1959). Rows of one year or less are blocks at
the midpoint; longer rows run first to last date; an empty when_end gets a dashed tail.
When each ledger search ran, for what purpose and with what result. The scroll-related searches run
from 1959 to 2009; most rows are manuscript surveys and excavations that report other finds.
How much ground a search covered or whether it reached any target: no row gives a target volume
(README). Date conflicts the README keeps open (S03, S04, S05, S13, S14) are not resolved. The
ledger's entry_ids are not drawn here.
